cues.en: I'm watching you.
cues.zh: 我在看着你。

cues.en: Lord Lord Kings, wow. It's it it it's such an honor. Indeed, sir. Please, just go. Just go right on through.
cues.zh: Lord Lord Kings，哇。真是，真是荣幸。确实，先生。请，直接进去吧。

cues.en: Woah. Woah. Identification,
cues.zh: 哇。哇。身份验证，

cues.en: please.
cues.zh: 请出示。

cues.en: Hik.
cues.zh: Hik。

cues.en: Nope. Hik.
cues.zh: 不对。Hik。

cues.en: Like,
cues.zh: 像是，

cues.en: high explosives.
cues.zh: 高爆炸药。

cues.en: High high explosives. Yeah.
cues.zh: 高，高爆炸药。对。

cues.en: We have a 1066
cues.zh: 我们有1066

cues.en: HQ. I repeat. We have a 1066.
cues.zh: 总部。重复。我们有1066。

cues.en: Copy that, Mike. What is a 1066? That was just an example of how to pronounce my name.
cues.zh: 收到，Mike。1066是什么？那只是示范一下我的名字怎么念。

cues.en: Ladies and gentlemen,
cues.zh: 女士们，先生们，

cues.en: members of the committee,
cues.zh: 委员会的成员们，

cues.en: we are here today to consider the impact
cues.zh: 今天我们来审议

cues.en: of government spending on our economy. We're fortunate to have two world renowned economists
cues.zh: 政府支出对我们经济的影响。我们很幸运有两位世界知名经济学家

cues.en: to offer their testimony on the matter.
cues.zh: 就此提供证词。

cues.en: I see you took a detour down the road to Serfdom. Talk about the end of laissez faire. Sheesh. Well, shaken off, Freddie. I'm not pulling any punches in there. I'm ready.
cues.zh: 我看你绕道走上了通往奴役之路。真是自由放任的终结啊。唉。行吧，Freddie，我已经甩开包袱了。我在里面可不会手下留情。我准备好了。

cues.en: Are you?
cues.zh: 你确定？

cues.en: Prepare for the return of the master.
cues.zh: 准备迎接大师回归。

cues.en: John Maynard Keynes,
cues.zh: John Maynard Keynes，

cues.en: FA Hayek,
cues.zh: FA Hayek，

cues.en: round two. Round
cues.zh: 第二回合。第

cues.en: Recession. Thanks to me. As you see, we're not in a depression. Recovery,
cues.zh: 衰退。多亏了我。如你所见，我们并没有陷入萧条。复苏，

cues.en: destiny. If you follow my lesson, Lord Caines, here I come. Line up for the procession. We brought out the shovels, we're still in a ditch and still digging. Don't you think it's time for a switch from that hair of the dog? Friend, the party is over. The long run is here. It's time to get sober. Are you kidding? Look, your work's perfectly fine. Have a look. The great recession ended back in o nine.
cues.zh: 命运。如果你听我的课，Keynes勋爵，我来了。排队迎接吧。我们拿出了铲子，我们还在坑里，还在挖。你不觉得该换个解酒法了吗？朋友，派对结束了。长期来了。该清醒了。你在开玩笑吗？你看，你的研究完全没问题。看看。大衰退早在09年就结束了。

cues.en: I deserve credit. Things wouldn't have been worse. All the estimates proven. I'll quote chapter and verse. Econometricians,
cues.zh: 我该得这份功劳，情况本可能更糟，所有预测都应验了。我可以引经据典来证明。那些计量经济学家，

cues.en: they're ever so biased. Are they doing real science or confirming their bias? Their Keynesian models are tidy and neat, but that top down approach is a fatal conceit.
cues.zh: 他们太有偏见了。他们是在做真正的科学，还是在确认自己的偏见？他们的凯恩斯模型整洁利落，但这种自上而下的方法是致命的傲慢。

cues.en: We could have done better had we only spent more. Too bad that only happens when there's a world war. You can carve all you want about stats and regression. Do you deny World War two cut short the depression? Wow. One data point and you're jumping for joy. The last time I checked, wars only destroy. There was no multiplier.
cues.zh: 要是我们多花点钱，本可以做得更好。可惜只有爆发世界大战时才会这样。你可以随便拿统计和回归来做文章。你否认二战缩短了大萧条吗？哇，就一个数据点你就欣喜若狂了。我上次查证过，战争只会带来毁灭。根本不存在乘数效应。

cues.en: Consumption just shrank as we used scarce resources for every new tank. Pretty perverse to call back prosperity.
cues.zh: 当我们把稀缺资源都用在每一辆新坦克上时，消费反而萎缩了。把复苏叫回来，这相当反常。

cues.en: Rationed meat, rationed butter, a life of austerity.
cues.zh: 肉类配给，黄油配给，紧缩度日的生活。

cues.en: When that war spending ended, your friends cried disaster.
cues.zh: 当战争支出结束时，你的朋友们大呼灾难临头。

cues.en: Yet the economy thrived and grew faster.
cues.zh: 然而经济繁荣了，增长更快了。

cues.en: You too only see what you want to see. The spending on war clearly goosed GDP.
cues.zh: 你也一样，只看到你想看到的。战争支出显然推高了GDP。

cues.en: Unemployment was over, almost down to zero. That's why I'm the master. That's why I'm the hero. Creating employ is a straightforward craft when the nation's at war and there's a draft. If every worker was staffed in the army and fleet, we'd have full employment and nothing to eat.
cues.zh: 失业问题解决了，几乎降到零。这就是为什么我是大师，这就是为什么我是英雄。当国家处于战争状态且有征兵时，创造就业是件直截了当的事。如果每个工人都被安排进军队和舰队，我们就会有充分就业，但没什么可吃的。

cues.en: Jobs are a means, not the ends in themselves. People work to live better, to put food on the shelves. Real growth means production of what people demand. That's entrepreneurship,
cues.zh: 工作是手段，而非目的本身。人们工作是为了生活得更好，为了把食物摆上货架。真正的增长意味着生产人们所需的东西。那才是创业精神，

cues.en: not your central plan. My solution is simple and easy to handle. It's spending that matters. Why is that such a scandal? Money sloshes through the pipes and the sluices,
cues.zh: 而不是你的中央计划。我的解决方案简单易行。重要的是支出。这有什么好大惊小怪的？资金流经管道和闸口，

cues.en: revitalizing the economy's juices. It's just like an engine that stalled and gone dark. To bring it to life, we need a quick spark. Spending's the life, but that gets the flow going.
cues.zh: 重振经济的活力。这就像一台熄火变暗的发动机。要让它活过来，我们需要一个快速的火花。支出是生命，但正是它让流动运转起来。

cues.en: Where it goes doesn't matter. Just get spending flowing. You'll see slack in some sectors as a general what. But some sectors are healthy, only some in a rush. So spending's not free. That's the heart of the matter. Too much is wasted as cronies get fatter. The economy's not a car. There's no engine to stall. No expert can fix it. There's no it at all. The economy is us. We don't need a mechanic. Put away the wrenches. The economy is organic.
cues.zh: 它流向哪里并不重要，关键是让消费流动起来。你会发现某些领域会出现松弛，作为一种普遍现象。但有些领域是健康的，只是有些在匆忙之中。所以消费并非免费，这才是问题的核心。太多资源被浪费，因为关系户越来越肥。经济不是一辆汽车，没有会熄火的引擎。没有专家能修好它，因为根本不存在那个“它”。经济就是我们自己，我们不需要修理工。把扳手收起来吧，经济是有机的。

cues.en: So what would you
cues.zh: 那么谁

cues.en: is who plans for whom? Do I plan for myself or leave it to you? I want plans by the many, not by the few. Let's not repeat what created our troubles. I want real growth, not a series of bubbles. Stop bailing out losers. Let's prices work. If we don't try to steer them, they won't go berserk. Come on. Are you kidding? Don't Wall Street gyrations challenge a worldview of self regulation?
cues.zh: 为谁做计划？我是为自己做计划，还是交给你来做？我要的是多数人的计划，而不是少数人的。我们不要再重蹈制造麻烦的覆辙。我要真正的增长，而不是一连串的泡沫。别再救助失败者了。让价格发挥作用吧。如果我们不去试图操纵它们，它们就不会失控。拜托。你在开玩笑吗？华尔街的波动难道不是在挑战自我监管的世界观吗？

cues.en: Even you must admit that the lesson we've learned is more oversight's needed or else we'll get burned. Oversight? The government's long been in bed with those Wall Street execs and the firms that they blend. Capitalism's
cues.zh: 即使是你也必须承认，我们得到的教训是需要更多监管，否则我们会被烧伤。监管？政府早就和那些华尔街高管以及他们勾连的公司同床共枕了。资本主义

cues.en: about profit and loss. You bail at the losers. There's no end to the cause. The lesson I've learned is how little we know. The world is complex, not some circular flow. The economy's not a class you can master in college. To think otherwise is the pretense of knowledge.
cues.zh: 关乎盈利与亏损。你救助失败者，因由就永无止境。我得到的教训是我们所知甚少。世界是复杂的，不是某种循环流动。经济不是你在大学里能掌握的一门课。不这样想，就是知识上的傲慢。

cues.en: On your high horse and you're off to the races. I look at the world on a case by case basis. When people are suffering, I roll up my sleeves and do what I can to cure our disease. The future's uncertain. Our outlooks are frail. That's why free markets are so prone to fail. In a volatile world, we need more discretion so state intervention can counter depression. People aren't chessmen you move on a board at your whim, their dreams and desires ignored.
cues.zh: 你高高在上，奔向赛场。我则逐案审视世界。当人们受苦时，我卷起袖子，尽力治愈我们的弊病。未来不确定，我们的前景脆弱。这就是自由市场容易失灵的原因。在动荡的世界里，我们需要更多自由裁量，让国家干预能对抗萧条。人不是棋盘上的棋子，任你随意摆布，他们的梦想和愿望被无视。

cues.en: With political incentives,
cues.zh: 在政治激励下，

cues.en: discretion's a joke. Those dials are twisting, just mirrors and smoke. We need stable rules and real market prices so prosperity emerges and cut short the crisis. Give us a chance so we can discover the most valuable way to serve one another.
cues.zh: 自由裁量是个笑话。那些旋钮在扭曲，不过是镜子和烟雾。我们需要稳定的规则和真实的市场价格，让繁荣涌现，缩短危机。给我们一个机会，让我们发现最有价值的互相服务方式。
